title: Requirements & scoping
strong: Asked 4–6 targeted questions, listed functional + non-functional requirements, explicitly cut scope, all in ≤ 8 min.
weak: Started coding immediately, or spent 15+ minutes asking questions without converging.

title: Entities & relationships
strong: Right nouns became classes, responsibilities are crisp, composition used over inheritance where it fits, relationships (1–N, has-a) are correct.
weak: God class, anemic data bags with logic elsewhere, or inheritance trees that would break on the next requirement.

title: Patterns & SOLID applied with reason
strong: Used 1–3 patterns where variation actually exists (Strategy for pricing, State for lifecycle…) and could say why.
weak: No abstraction at the points of change, or pattern-stuffing (Singleton + Factory + Visitor for no reason).

title: Working, readable code
strong: Core flows compile and work, names are clear, methods are short, no dead code, sensible packages/types. Hidden tests mostly green.
weak: Did not compile or only skeletons, long methods, magic numbers, unclear naming.

title: Edge cases, errors & concurrency
strong: Validated inputs, defined failure behaviour (exceptions/errors), identified shared state and protected it (locks/atomic/channels) where needed.
weak: Happy path only, or a double-booking/race that was never considered.

title: Communication & extensibility
strong: Narrated trade-offs, managed time, and answered the 'now add X' follow-up by pointing at the exact class to extend.
weak: Silent coding, defensive about feedback, or a follow-up required rewriting the core.
